To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

(1) the accuracy of genome-based breeding value estimation depends on heritability, QTL dispersion, QTL size and the accuracy with which QTL are located; (2) the accuracy of QTL position estimation is dependent on the accuracy of genome based breeding value estimation; and (3) the accuracy of the estimation of QTL size is dependent on the number of QTL.
genome-wide estimated breeding values are feasible for a wide range of heritabilities and QTL effects and sizes, and that QTL positions can be estimated to within a few centimorgans.

genome-wide estimated breeding values are possible with a half-sib design, but that the accuracy of the estimated breeding values is influenced by the dispersion of QTL across the genome and the size of QTL effects.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the development of methods to estimate the effects of DNA segments on traits of interest.
the use of SNP panels to estimate haplotype effects and genome-wide estimated breeding values in a half-sib design.
the estimation of the effects of haplotypes of DNA on a trait or set of traits of interest.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
genome-wide estimated breeding values are possible and can be used in selection programs to improve the accuracy of selection.
the accuracy of genome wide selection is high enough to make it a viable approach to genetic improvement in the future.
the use of haplotypes for genome-wide selection in a half-sib design is feasible and can give high accuracies of selection.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
genome-wide selection using a granddaughter design is feasible, and can be done with a reasonable amount of accuracy, even when QTL positions are not known.
genome-wide estimated breeding values based on SNP intervals are a viable alternative to the traditional single locus QTL analysis for half-sib populations.
haplotype interval estimation is a viable approach for estimating genome-wide breeding values.
The main takeaway from our work is that
genome-wide estimated breeding values are feasible and can be computed in a reasonable amount of time.
genome-wide selection is feasible and should be investigated in livestock populations with a high density of SNP.
genome-wide estimated breeding values are accurate enough for use in a breeding program.
